biggest_leak: The email gate (leak #1) — ~56% of scanners never give an email; it is the owner's #1 target and gates every downstream reward. But because a bold structural fix to it is business-impacting and depends on mechanics I cannot verify, AND the leak is currently unmeasurable in a frozen window (PostHog 403 + durable page_viewed only 2 days live), this cycle attacks it by making it measurable and diagnosable from durable truth rather than shipping a blind guess.

diagnosis.question: Why do the ~56% of people who scan the QR and reach the claim page not submit an email?
hypotheses_considered: H1 Never intended to — the discount is for a NEXT order; a one-off gift buyer may not want one (ceiling on this leak).
H2 Unwilling to trade an email for something pitched as no-strings on the box.
H3 Don't understand or trust the offer — asked for an address before receiving anything, no on-page proof the reward is real (and there is genuinely no code to show: codes are unique/single-use).
H4 Never reached the field — bounced, slow load, confused.
H5 Tried and failed — typo, validation error, keyboard/form friction.
diagnosis.evidence_gathered: Analysed PostHog session-recording METADATA (keypress_count, click_count, console_error_count, recording_duration, start_url) for 186 claim-page sessions this window and 195 in the prior window (offset-paginated; a capped sample, not a census — I did not visually watch each replay, I read the interaction counters across the whole sample, which is the reproducible way to separate engaged from not-engaged). Also read the cached PostHog full-journey funnel (1864->826) and the Supabase daily event counts.
diagnosis.what_the_evidence_supports: The leak is dominated by people who REACH the page and DECLINE, not people who never arrive or who fail the form. Only 28/186 (15%) bounce in <5s (H4 minor); console errors are near zero — 2/186 — and a third of sessions do type, so H5 (tried-and-failed) is small. The remaining ~97 never-typers spent a meaningful 5-90s+ on the page and 51 clicked/scrolled without ever typing an email. That behaviour — engaged, considered, left without giving an email — is consistent with H2 (won't trade the email) and/or H3 (don't trust/understand the pre-payment ask), and the pattern is stable across both windows.
diagnosis.what_it_cannot_distinguish: The metadata CANNOT separate H1 (never wanted a next-order discount) from H2 (won't give an email) from H3 (don't trust the offer) — all three produce the same 'engaged then left without typing' signature. It also can't confirm, among the 61 typers, how many abandoned vs submitted. And crucially, none of this is currently answerable from DURABLE truth in a frozen, person-linked, significance-testable way: the claim page logs a page view (2 days old) and a submit and NOTHING in between, and the replay source that filled the gap this cycle is capped/sampled and access-fragile (the same PostHog key just 403'd on the query API). That fragility is the case for shipping durable instrumentation this cycle.

plan.title: Durable claim-page diagnostic instrumentation: log first email-field engagement (+ make page_viewed bounce-proof) so the biggest leak becomes measurable and diagnosable from Supabase truth
plan.targets: The email gate (claim page_view -> email_entered) — instrumenting it, not yet changing it.
plan.mechanism: Add ONE new durable funnel event, `email_field_engaged` (phase=claim, source=claim_page), fired once the first time the user focuses/taps the claim email input. Combined with the already-live `page_viewed` and `email_entered`, the next cycles can compute two person-linked, frozen, significance-tested sub-steps: (1) page_viewed -> email_field_engaged = 'did they engage the field at all?' (isolates H4 never-reached / never-considered), and (2) email_field_engaged -> email_entered = 'of those who engaged, who submitted?' (isolates H5 tried-and-gave-up from H2/H3 considered-and-declined). This turns the single 'page view -> submit, nothing between' gap into a 3-step diagnosis on the durable source of truth, independent of PostHog query access (which failed this cycle) and of capped replay sampling. Also add `keepalive: true` to the two existing claim /api/track POSTs (page_viewed, email_entered) so <5s bounces — 15% of sessions — still record and the denominator is trustworthy.
plan.assumed_cause: No single cause is assumed — the change is explicitly a diagnosis-enabler that bets ONLY on the well-supported observation that the leak is decision-stage ('engaged then declined'), not arrival or form-failure, and that the competing decision-stage hypotheses (H1/H2/H3) need one more durable signal to start separating. It commits to no copy/offer theory.
plan.expected_effect: No conversion change expected or claimed. Success = next cycle can run `node --experimental-websocket tools/linked-funnel.mjs page_viewed email_field_engaged 14 --until=... --compare` and `... email_field_engaged email_entered ...` and get real per-person rates with significance, quantifying how much of the ~56% loss is never-engaged vs engaged-and-declined — from durable truth, without depending on the PostHog query scope that 403'd this cycle.

tradeoff.gained: The biggest leak in the funnel becomes measurable and partially diagnosable from the durable source of truth, hardened against the exact failure that blinded this cycle (PostHog query 403 + replay being a capped sample). Enables the next 3+ cycles to target the email gate with evidence instead of a guess.
tradeoff.risked: Almost none: purely additive client logging, no user-facing/layout change, best-effort fetch that never blocks. The only real cost is one cycle's build spent on measurement rather than a conversion change — accepted because a blind conversion change here would be ungradeable right now and is the over-claim trap this role exists to avoid. Downstream review-click volume is unaffected (this change touches nothing in the email/Klaviyo path). For reference, the Klaviyo review-reminder path (phase=email_redirect) produced 0 review clicks this window and 2 in the prior window, so it is a small but real share of the ~8-10 total review clicks/fortnight — relevant to any FUTURE email-gate change, not to this one.
unverified_assumptions: OWNER QUESTION (for a future bold fix, NOT this cycle): can an UNASSIGNED code be pulled from the Klaviyo `PrizeForms` pool and shown on the claim page at scan time WITHOUT an email, given Klaviyo assigns codes to profiles? If yes, the 'give the discount first, ask email second' structural fix becomes viable. I could not verify this from the code or data and did not assume it.

OWNER QUESTION: is it acceptable for pool codes to be 'burned' on scanners who never convert (pool depletion)? `PrizeForms` is described as almost entirely unassigned, but the depletion rate under scan-time issuance is unknown.

OWNER QUESTION: can the PostHog personal API key be regranted the `query:read` scope? Without it, tools/posthog-funnel.mjs (presets/funnel/trend/hogql) cannot run, so the top-of-funnel is measurable ONLY once the new durable events accumulate ~2 weeks. This is the single biggest measurement blocker right now.

plan.differs_from_past_attempt: NOT PR #8 (which rebuilt the claim page with a two-reward layout/hierarchy and left capture flat 44.5%->39.0%): this ships ZERO presentation/layout change — no new copy, no reordering, no visual element — only additive event logging. It is also NOT the owner-rejected 'name the printed-vs-actual discount gap' proposal (it references no percentage and nothing about the print). And it is not the 'remove/defer the email gate' structural change (which is business-impacting, depends on the unverified Klaviyo mechanics above, and is surfaced here only as owner questions). It is the 'make the next cycles able to see' output the FUNNEL_CONTEXT instrumentation note explicitly blesses as often superior.
plan.how_to_verify: Build then: (1) load claim.html locally with a test SKU, focus the email input once, and confirm exactly one `email_field_engaged` row (phase=claim, source=claim_page) lands in log_video_funnel_events and that re-focusing does NOT duplicate it; confirm `page_viewed` and `email_entered` still land; then delete the test rows I created. (2) Confirm api/track.js needs no change — it already inserts any `event` string with no whitelist (verified). (3) Next cycle (~2026-08-03): run `node --experimental-websocket tools/linked-funnel.mjs page_viewed email_field_engaged 14 --until=2026-08-03 --compare` and `... email_field_engaged email_entered ...`, then significance-test each; the entry ships as INFRA / measurable:false and will NEVER be given a worked/worse verdict.
alternatives_rejected: Ship a bold email-gate structural change now (show a code at scan / defer the email): highest potential prize but business-impacting, depends on unverified Klaviyo code-without-email mechanics (owner questions above), and — decisively — would be UNGRADEABLE this cycle because the top-of-funnel is currently unmeasurable (PostHog 403 + page_viewed 2 days old). Shipping an unmeasurable bold change into a measurement blackout is the over-claim risk this role must avoid. Surfaced as an owner recommendation instead.

A claim-page copy/trust tweak (e.g. clarify what the email delivers): can never be proven at ~12-16 landers/day (noise floor ~13-20pts), and is presentation-shaped — adjacent to the spent PR #8 ground. Rejected.

Do nothing / carry all leaks forward: defensible, but wastes the cycle when a concrete, low-risk instrumentation gap is blocking evidence-based work on the #1 leak and PostHog access just proved fragile. Shipping the durable signal is strictly better than another blind pending cycle.

Also add scroll-depth and time-to-first-interaction events: deferred to keep the change surgical; first email-field engagement is the single most decision-relevant missing signal and separates the key hypotheses on its own.
